operations.title: Five-site projective Krylov numerator-degree typing audit
The order-six Krylov ladder is numerator-degree-starved and does not yet constrain Gauss–Manin rank
operations.summary: The base rational coefficient has numerator degree 11, the descended denominator has u-degree at most 90, but the tested exact primitives stop at degree 3. Linear rank growth through order six is therefore only a valid low-degree exclusion and cannot be promoted to evidence for a high-rank module.

operations.title: Nima corrects the rank interpretation of the projective Krylov ladder
operations.body: Degree audit: the 26-factor descended denominator has u-degree <=90 (support census 1 zero, 5 single, 20 double), while the known weight-five numerator already has degree 11 and our primitive ansatz stopped at degree 3. Thus the order 1..6 zero-relation table remains a valid low-degree exclusion, but its +4 rank growth is not evidence for high Gauss-Manin rank. The next gate is a reduction-compatible numerator filtration or sparse polynomial-module basis, not order 7.
